newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taipei city sets midnight curfew for youths.
newsitem.headline: Taipei city sets midnight curfew for youths.

text.p: Three months after sweeping away many of Taipei's prostitutes, crusading mayor Chen Shui-bian wants to clear the capital of another street-walking group -- juveniles.
Police chief Ting Yuan-ching said on Thursday that Chen ordered him immediately to begin enforcing a curfew banning children under 18 from public arenas after midnight.
Ting said at a year-end press conference that the government decided to institute the curfew after studies showed that most crimes committed against and by juveniles occurred late at night.

"Any youngster caught on the streets after midnight without an accompanying parent will be taken to a nearby police station," Ting said. "The station then will contact a parent to take the child home."
Youths caught in prostitution-related activities would be sent to juvenile counselling centres, Ting said.

Chen dismissed critics who saw the curfew as a civil rights violation incompatible with Taiwan's decade-old democratic awakening, saying New York and several other U.S. cities had enacted similar restrictions with excellent results.

Chen, who in 1994 became the first member of an opposition party elected mayor of Taiwan's capital city, has made it a priority of his administration to rid Taipei of its notorious red-light districts, gangsters and juvenile crime.
Police shut down more than 200 Taipei sex parlours operating in residential areas in a broad September crackdown. Few have reopened.
